institution: Schools in Safed (Mandatory Palestine) and Damascus (Syria)
detail: According to his official biography, he began school in Safed, which his family left during the 1948 war, and as a refugee in Damascus worked to help support his family, continued his education at home and eventually attended high school.
His official biography states that he completed a law degree at the University of Damascus in 1958; Britannica also records a law degree from Damascus.

institution: Moscow (Soviet Union): Institute of Oriental Studies of the USSR Academy of Sciences; sources differ on the awarding institution
qualification: Candidate of Sciences (kandidat nauk, the Soviet equivalent of a PhD)
detail: Britannica states that he was awarded a doctorate in history in 1982 after defending his dissertation at the Institute of Oriental Studies in Moscow; Wikipedia describes the degree as a Candidate of Sciences prepared at the Patrice Lumumba Peoples' Friendship University and defended at the Institute of Oriental Studies, while his official biography says the doctorate was awarded by the Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO). The dissertation, on relations between Nazism and the leaders of the Zionist movement in 1933–1945, was published in 1984 as the book 'The Other Side' and has been criticised by Jewish groups as Holocaust denial (see polemics).
